text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Carrefour retail group increases stake in holding GMB, which controls supermarket group Cora, to over 40 percent, chairman Philippe Bouriez says in an interview. Says remaining family shareholders of GMB determined not to sell their stakes. Adds Cora offered a 1.2 billion franc standby loan by Credit National.
-- President Jacques Chirac calls for further savings at ministries, which he sees as a key to lowering taxes.
-- LVMH luxury goods group to buy U.S. retailer DFS for some 13 billion francs, would increase LVMH 1997 profit by 30 percent. Still needs clearance from U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
-- Bank of France cuts overnight lending rate to 3.25.
-- EDF electricity supplier to cut prices by six percent from February 1997 to improve competitivity ahead of market deregulation.
-- Employers and unions negotiate 1997 unemployment benefits, diverge over use of a 13-billion-franc excess at Unedic unemployment fund expected in 1997 and 1998.
-- Usinor Sacilor offer on Spain's steel maker CSI's privatisation regarded favourably by Spanish authorities.
-- Societe Generale to spin off its portfolio management activities into subsidiaries.
-- European ministers of telecommunications reach agreement on postal industry deregulation, allowing a balance between free enterprise and public service.

-- European commissionner Karel Van Miert says French state help plan for textile sector is similar to a Belgian plan which was forbidden by the EU commission in December, implying an eventual denial of approval.
-- Banque Lazard unit Eurafrance launches buyout offer on outstanding 41 percent stake of its insurance subsidiary La France, considers merging Eurafrance and La France.
-- National Assembly does not rule out a planned merger of nuclear plant maker Framatome with GEC Alsthom provided Parliament keeps a control over the French nuclear industry.
